title: Ferenc Wesselényi to Leopold I(?), cipher passages in a Latin draft, c. 1663-64 (DECODE R674)

documents.shelfmark: MNL OL E 199 (Wesselényi family archive), 8. pallium 1. 01 (DECODE R674)
documents.date: undated (c. 1663-64; DECODE 1 Jan 1664 is the start of a 1664-1670 span)
documents.route: Ferenc Wesselényi -> King Leopold I (inferred from 'Maiestatis Vestrae')

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the page or in print; read here.

transcription.source: DECODE transcription DOC_R674_D1892 (EK, 2020), checked against image IMG_R674_I4003
transcription.notes: One correction: after 'prius' the first number is 10, not 20. DECODE's b/g/i/o letters are 6/9/1/0.

system.summary: Reversed-alphabet substitution on numbers 1-24 (24=a ... 1=z) with vowel homophones 25=a, 26=e, 28=o, 29=u and a few higher code numbers (60, 64) for names or places; word runs embedded in Latin clear text.
system.sibling_key: DECODE R672 (MNL OL P 1238 Teleki collection, cipher keys no. 12): same reversed alphabet, but syllables Ba-Bu at 25-29 and Ka-Ku at 60-64; found after the reading, confirms the letters, does not give the codes.
system.notes: Writer's slip: 9 (q) for p once in 'Spork'.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie and /goal target setting. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Fetched R674 metadata, image and DECODE transcription with the saved cookie.
Parsed DECODE transcription into 244 number tokens (b/g/i/o -> 6/9/1/0); checked against the image, one correction (10 not 20 after 'prius').
Unconstrained homophonic anneal with Latin and Hungarian 4-gram LMs.
One-to-one anneal: Latin impossible (21-letter model, 25 symbols); Hungarian gave pseudo-Hungarian.
Latin anneal with at most two numbers per letter: all 8 seeds give readable Latin (tria millia hominum constituere, praesidium maiestatis vestrae reciperent).
Fixed key by hand from 'si Dominus Generalis', tria millia hominum, duo millia peditum; names Haster (Heister), Snaidau (Schneidau), Spork; nux (3=x), ab indusio.
Web search for a printed edition or prior decipherment of the draft.
Fetched R675 and keys R665-R673, R676-R690; scored each against the recovered values. R672 has the same reversed alphabet (19 agreements); its 60/64 (Ka/Ku) do not fit.
Re-decoded every run with the final key; all Latin in context. Codes 60, 64 left unread.

outcome.method_basis: The reversed-alphabet key was recovered by Latin annealing with at most two numbers per letter and fixed by hand from probable words; DECODE key R672 (Teleki collection), found afterwards, has the same alphabet but different codes.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md / decode_out.txt: 244 cipher tokens, 241 letters read, codes 60 (x1) and 64 (x2) unread.

gaps.detail: once; not in R672 or any Teleki / Fasc. 327 key
twice; a place that might take an imperial garrison

outcome.notes: Whole draft read ciphertext-only; alphabet later confirmed by DECODE key R672. Open: two code numbers.
